title: Collection of tax at source by seller on receipt of consideration for sale of goods (Omitted effective 1 April 2025)

effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: CRITICAL SUNSET: Section 206C(1H) is formally omitted by Finance Act, 2025 effective 1 April 2025. Post-sunset, seller TCS on sale of goods ceases entirely. Tax withholding on sale of goods is governed strictly by buyer TDS under Section 194Q where the buyer independently satisfies Section 194Q threshold criteria (prior year turnover exceeding ₹10 Crore and cumulative purchases exceeding ₹50 Lakhs). If the buyer is not liable under Section 194Q, no withholding tax or collection of tax attaches to the sale of goods.

plainTextSummary: Prior to 1 April 2025, a seller whose turnover exceeded ₹10 Crore in the preceding financial year was required to collect 0.1% TCS on receipts exceeding ₹50 Lakhs from a buyer, unless the buyer was liable to deduct TDS under Section 194Q and had deducted such tax. Effective 1 April 2025, Section 206C(1H) is omitted by the Finance Act, 2025 to eliminate double-compliance overlap. Following this omission, seller TCS on goods is obsolete; buyer TDS under Section 194Q applies only where the buyer independently satisfies its statutory prerequisites.

keyStatutoryThresholds.precedenceRule: Historically prior to 1 April 2025, Section 194Q buyer TDS took statutory precedence over Section 206C(1H) seller TCS when the buyer was compliant.

officialCitations.authority: Parliament of India / Ministry of Finance
